description: GDU (Gross Domestic Usage) as a benefit-based alternative to GDP: evidence that measurement concepts feed back into economic reality, and the GDP-B framework as methodological foundation. Draft to be validated against json_structure.md.

words.name: gdp-b
words.description: GDP extended by benefits of new and free goods, estimated via incentive-compatible choice experiments (Brynjolfsson et al.)

words.name: performativity
words.description: economic models act as engines shaping markets, not cameras depicting them (MacKenzie)

words.name: USD
words.description: Is a symbol for US dollar

words.name: value
words.description: a stored number; reference the provenance qualifier triple, not this bare word

triples.name: policy priorities
triples.description: what a government steers for, shaped by the metric it measures

triples.name: welfare measure
triples.description: a metric of welfare rather than of market turnover

triples.name: gross domestic usage
triples.description: GDU: period-over-period change in usage/benefit, measuring prevention of unhappiness rather than market turnover

triples.name: measurement feedback
triples.description: the chosen metric changes the measured system: policy steering, Goodhart's law, performativity

triples.name: goodharts law
triples.description: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure

triples.name: willingness to accept
triples.description: compensation demanded to give up access to a good; welfare measure for zero-price goods

triples.name: facebook wta
triples.description: median monthly willingness to accept for giving up Facebook, US 2016-17

triples.name: gdp-b growth contribution facebook
triples.description: annual percentage-point addition to US GDP-B growth 2004-2017 from including Facebook

triples.name: smartphone camera wta
triples.description: median monthly willingness to accept for giving up the smartphone camera, NL lab study 2017

triples.name: taxi example
triples.description: GDU illustration: app cuts taxi prices 20 percent, usage rises 10 percent, GDP falls while benefit rises

triples.name: encyclopedia example
triples.description: GDU illustration: Wikipedia replaces paid encyclopedias, GDP vanishes while usage explodes

triples.name: air pollution example
triples.description: GDU illustration: GDP doubles while unpriced clean-up cost exceeds the gain, so GDU falls

sources.name: Brynjolfsson et al. 2019
sources.description: Brynjolfsson, Collis, Diewert, Eggers, Fox (2019): GDP-B: Accounting for the Value of New and Free Goods in the Digital Economy. NBER WP 25695. Incentive-compatible choice experiments; Facebook median WTA USD 42.17/month; GDP-B growth contribution 0.05-0.11 pp/year; smartphone camera median WTA EUR 68.13/month vs USD 20-35 manufacturing cost; names Wikipedia replacing encyclopedias as an example of GDP missing free-good welfare.

sources.name: Stiglitz Fitoussi Durand 2018
sources.description: Beyond GDP: Measuring What Counts for Economic and Social Performance. OECD. Central message: what we measure affects what we do; GDP over-reliance contributed to policymakers missing the 2008 crisis and to inadequate crisis response.

sources.name: Strathern 1997
sources.description: Improving ratings: audit in the British University system. European Review 5(3), 305-321. Formulation of Goodhart's law: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.

sources.name: MacKenzie 2006
sources.description: An Engine, Not a Camera: How Financial Models Shape Markets. MIT Press. Black-Scholes case: option prices converged toward model predictions after publication (performativity).

sources.name: zukunft.com GDU text
sources.description: GDU concept text by Timon Zielonka: benefit per capita / prevention of unhappiness; taxi, encyclopedia, and air pollution examples.

values.description: 95% CI 33.53 to 136.78; order of magnitude above USD 20-35 manufacturing cost
usage rises 10 percent while sector GDP falls 12 percent (10 to 8.8 mio USD); confidence 0.9 as illustrative arithmetic
annual German Wikipedia page views; replaces ~30 mio paid look-ups at ~2 EUR each (60 mio EUR / 300k buyers x 100 uses); confidence 0.6
GDU change in USD: GDP gain 1000 mio minus unpriced clean-up cost 1200 mio; confidence 0.9 as illustrative arithmetic
